title: Emaar India — Risk & Reputation Research
content:
According to Trustpilot reviews, Emaar India is rated "Bad" with 1.4 out of 5 stars. Customers have reported poor customer service, rude behavior from the maintenance team, and issues with property quality, including a damaged window left unaddressed for over a year. One reviewer from Gurgaon, Haryana, described the company's customer service as "0% customer care, just words" and recommended legal support when dealing with Emaar. Another reviewer mentioned complications in contacting Emaar for issues with their apartment at Creek Beach, which had many problems despite being less than a year old.

The icing on the cake is their Rude behaviour. Each one of the maintenance team members fight to stay ahead of each another in terms of gobsmacked behaviour with the residents, once they shift to the property.  
  
In totality it's absolutely useless hammering your brains after buying in Emaar.   
Never ever invest with this company's townships.  
  
BTW, I'm from India ( Gurgaon, Haryana ) & is experiencing this awfull service in Emaar Emedald Floors Premier. [...] ## worst customer treatment I ever…
worst customer treatment I ever experienced ever.   
I am left since around 1 year with a damaged window, since handover of the property in creek rise 2. The company is putting the health and safety of their customer at risk!!! Customer service is not able to take any action, is misinformed, full of excuses and lies.   
I highly recommend to get leagal support when dealing with EMAAR.

January 14, 2024

The sources indicate mixed experiences with Emaar India regarding delivery delays and service quality. Historical customer experience from the Emaar MGF era includes delivery delays of three to five years beyond original timelines, construction-quality concerns, and slow resolution of snagging issues. Emaar India has delivered some projects on time, such as Emaar The Palm Drive and Emaar Gurgaon Greens, but others faced significant delays, like the house in Emaar South that was delayed by 2.5 years. Complaints also include lack of transparency during delays, aggressive upselling, and resale challenges. The sources do not provide a definitive answer on the current status of delivery delays and service quality in 2026.

Our research describes a mixed historical customer experience, particularly from the Emaar MGF era.

#### Opportunities

## Delivery Track Record: The Numbers Don't Lie

One of the biggest concerns with any builder is delivery timelines. Emaar India has had a mixed track record here.

### On-Time Deliveries

To their credit, Emaar delivered several projects without major delays:

 Emaar The Palm Drive: Promised 2012, delivered 2012-2013 (on time)
 Emaar Digi Homes: Promised 2015, delivered 2015-2016 (minor delays of 3-6 months)
 Emaar Gurgaon Greens: Promised 2014, delivered 2014-2015 (largely on time) [...] Lack of transparency during delays: Buyers in The Views project report minimal communication during the 7-year delay period.
 Aggressive upselling: Emaar staff are known to push upgrades, parking slots, and club memberships aggressively during the booking process.
 Resale challenges: Under-construction Emaar flats often see 10-20% depreciation in resale value due to buyer skepticism around delivery timelines. [...] PropReport's automated due diligence checks pull RERA data, construction progress, legal clearances, and buyer reviews to flag these risks before you commit.

## Final Thoughts: Emaar India in 2026

Emaar India is a reliable builder with a mixed recent track record. Their older projects (2010-2016 era) were delivered on time with solid build quality. Newer projects (2017-2023) faced significant delays, though most eventually got completed.

The Delhi State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, presided over by Justice Sangita Dhingra Sehgal (President) and Ms. Bimla Kumari (Member), has dismissed the complaint filed by homebuyers against Emaar India Limited, finding that no cause of action survived once the buyers accepted possession of the unit and received delay compensation. [...] The Commission therefore dismissed the complaint on the grounds that it was filed after all obligations had been discharged, and no claim lay thereafter. All pending applications were also disposed of. With the complainants having accepted possession and delay compensation without contest, the Delhi State Consumer Commission held that there was no ongoing cause of action. Accordingly, the complaint against Emaar India Limited was dismissed in its entirety.

Emaar India has faced several reputation problems and criticism, particularly noted in delayed projects and aggressive upselling practices. Buyers in The Views project reported minimal communication during a 7-year delay period. Emaar staff are known to push upgrades aggressively during the booking process. Post-2016, Emaar's track record became shakier with delays in projects like Emaar MGF The Views and Emaar Urban Ascent. Reported complaints include delivery delays of three to five years beyond original timelines, construction-quality concerns, and slow resolution of post-possession snagging. The demerger period between 2016 and 2020 was particularly difficult for some buyers due to transition in project management. Additionally, Emaar India has faced legal issues, including a notice served by Gurugram banks over false information on layout and an FIR registered against Emaar Properties PJSC and its Indian subsidiary, Emaar India Ltd, for selling a green belt plot to build a school.

### Delayed Projects

However, post-2016, Emaar's track record became shakier:

 Emaar MGF The Views (Sector 105A): Originally slated for 2018 possession, still incomplete as of May 2026. Buyers report possession delays of 7+ years with minimal updates from the builder.
 Emaar Urban Ascent (Sector 112): Promised 2020, delivered late 2023 — a 3-year delay. [...] 1. RERA compliance delays: Post-2016, RERA registration slowed many projects across Gurugram.
2. Funding issues: Emaar MGF (the JV entity) reportedly faced internal restructuring and funding challenges around 2017-2020.
3. Infrastructure dependencies: Projects along Dwarka Expressway were contingent on road completion, which itself faced delays until 2024.

Bottom line: If you're buying an under-construction Emaar property, build in a 2-3 year buffer beyond the promised possession date.
